Connect your **Hikvision IP cameras and recorders (NVR / DVR)** to Gladys, **on your local
network**: camera images, real-time detections (motion, line crossing, intrusion, tampering…), alarm
inputs and outputs, PTZ, scenes and a dashboard widget.

- **Local only**: Gladys talks directly to each device through its ISAPI. No Hik-Connect account, no
  cloud, nothing to open on your router.
- **One recorder brings all its cameras**: add the address of the NVR, not each camera behind it.

## What you need

- Gladys **5.1 or later**.
- A Hikvision camera or recorder on the same network as Gladys, with a fixed IP address (DHCP
  reservation).
- A user account on that device (see below).

## 1. Prepare the device

In the web interface of the camera or recorder:

1. **Create a dedicated user**: _Configuration > System > User Management > Add_. Give it the
   **Operator** role. Avoid using `admin`: Gladys does not need it.
   - To let Gladys switch detections on and off (arm / disarm), the user needs the right to change
     the settings ("Parameters Settings" / remote configuration).
2. **Enable the ISAPI**: _Configuration > Network > Advanced Settings > Integration Protocol_ — tick
   **Enable Hikvision-CGI** with the **Digest** authentication. On recent firmwares it is enabled by
   default.
3. **Note the HTTP port** (_Network > Basic Settings > Port_) if it is not 80.

> **Careful with passwords**: Hikvision locks the account (often for 30 minutes) after a few wrong
> passwords. The integration therefore never retries a refused password by itself: fix it, then
> save the configuration again (or press **Test the connection**).

## 2. Configure the integration

In Gladys: _Integrations > Hikvision > Configuration_.

| Field                       | What to enter                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Addresses                   | IP address of each camera or recorder, separated by commas: `192.168.1.64, 192.168.1.70:8080`. Add `https://` for HTTPS.                 |
| User name / Password        | The account created above. The same account is used on every device.                                                                     |
| Check the HTTPS certificate | Leave off: Hikvision devices use a self-signed certificate.                                                                              |
| Snapshot interval (s)       | How often each camera's image is refreshed in Gladys (60 s by default, 10 s minimum, 0 = only when Gladys asks).                         |
| Image quality               | **Sub-stream** (recommended). Gladys accepts images up to 150 KB; the main stream is reduced to 1280×720, and replaced if still too big. |
| Detection hold (s)          | How long a detection stays "on" after the last event of the camera (10 s by default).                                                    |
| Health check interval (s)   | How often each device is checked (60 s by default).                                                                                      |
| Detailed logs               | Turn on to diagnose, then off again.                                                                                                     |

Save, then press **Test the connection**: one line per device tells the model, the firmware, the
cameras online, the detections found, whether events are received live, and the alarm inputs and
outputs. When something is wrong, the line says what to do.

Then open the **Discover** tab and create the devices you want.

## 3. The devices in Gladys

**One device per camera** (a camera has one, a recorder one per camera behind it):

| Feature                   | Type          | Notes                                                           |
| ------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Image                     | camera        | refreshed at the snapshot interval, and on demand               |
| Motion                    | motion sensor | always present                                                  |
| Line crossing / Intrusion | motion sensor | when the camera supports these smart detections                 |
| Tampering                 | tamper        | when the camera supports it                                     |
| Motion / … detection      | switch        | turns that detection on or off **on the camera** (arm / disarm) |
| PTZ                       | camera move   | PTZ cameras only: short pan / tilt / zoom steps, always stopped |
| Preset                    | camera preset | PTZ cameras with saved presets: the list comes from the camera  |

**One "alarm I/O" device per camera or recorder that has dry contacts**: each **alarm input** is a
binary input (1 while in alarm), each **alarm output** (relay, siren) is a switch.

Each device shows a **local** badge when it answers, **unreachable** otherwise. An orange dot means
the device answers but its event stream is not connected: detections do not arrive.

## 4. Scenes

### Triggers

- **A Hikvision camera detects something** — filters: the camera, the event (motion, line crossing,
  intrusion, region entrance / exiting, tampering, face, scene change, unattended or removed object,
  PIR, video loss, alarm input) and, for smart events, the target (person or vehicle). Fired once per
  detection, not for every repeat of the camera. Variables: `event_type`, `target`, `device_name`,
  `channel`, `description`.
- **A Hikvision camera goes offline** / **is back online** — variables: `device_name` (and `reason`
  when going offline).

The detection features (Motion, Intrusion…) can also be used with the standard "device state"
trigger.

### Actions

- **Take a Hikvision snapshot** — captures the image now. Put it right before the Gladys action
  "Send a camera image" to receive the very moment of the detection. Output: `captured`.
- **Arm or disarm a Hikvision detection** — switches a detection (motion, line crossing, intrusion,
  tampering) of a camera on or off. Outputs: `applied`, `enabled`.
- **Move a Hikvision PTZ camera to a preset** — preset number as saved on the camera. Output:
  `moved`.

Example: _When an intrusion with target "person" is detected by the Garden camera, and nobody is
home → take a snapshot → send the camera image → switch the siren (alarm output) on._

## 5. Dashboard widget

Add the **Hikvision** widget to a dashboard: cameras online, detections of the last 24 hours, the
image of a camera (the one chosen in the widget settings, or by default the one that detected
something last) and the last detection of each camera. Buttons: **Snapshot**, **Disarm** and
**Arm** (all the detections of every camera, after confirmation).

## Troubleshooting

| Problem                                 | Solution                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "user name or password refused"         | Check them in the web interface of the device. If the account got locked, wait about 30 minutes, then save the configuration again.                     |
| "the device does not answer the ISAPI"  | Enable the integration protocol (step 1.2).                                                                                                             |
| "this user lacks the rights"            | Give the user the Operator role, or the right to change parameters.                                                                                     |
| No detection arrives                    | Check that the detection is enabled on the camera **and** that "Notify surveillance center" is ticked in its linkage method. Turn on the detailed logs. |
| "the snapshot is over the 150 KB"       | Lower the sub-stream resolution of the camera (e.g. 640×360).                                                                                           |
| A camera behind the recorder is offline | Gladys shows it unreachable and fires "goes offline"; it comes back by itself.                                                                          |
| HTTPS refused                           | Use `http://` or untick "Check the HTTPS certificate"; check the port.                                                                                  |

## Privacy and security

Everything stays between Gladys and your devices, on your network. The password is stored in a
secret field of Gladys and never written to the logs. The integration keeps in its `/data` folder
only what it learnt from the devices (model, serial number, channels) so that a device that is off
at startup still shows up as offline.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Hikvision asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | Everything stays on your network: Gladys talks to each camera or recorder (NVR) over its local ISAPI, no Hik-Connect account needed. Create a dedicated user on the device (Operator role), check that the integration protocol (ISAPI) is enabled, then enter the address of each device below. |
| Addresses | `string` | Yes | IP address (or name) of each camera or recorder, separated by commas. Add the port when it is not 80, and https:\/\/ for HTTPS. A recorder brings all its cameras: do not add them as well. |
| User name | `string` | Yes | The same account on every device. A dedicated Operator user is better than admin. |
| Password | `secret` | Yes | Hikvision locks the account after a few wrong passwords: a refused password is not retried until you save the configuration again. |
| Check the HTTPS certificate | `boolean` | No | Only for https:\/\/ addresses. Hikvision devices ship a self-signed certificate: leave this off unless you installed a certificate Gladys trusts. |
| Snapshot interval (s) | `number` | No | How often each camera's image is refreshed in Gladys, in seconds (10 minimum). 0 turns it off: Gladys then gets an image only when it asks for one. |
| Image quality | `select` | No | Gladys accepts images up to 150 KB. The sub-stream always fits; the main stream is reduced to 1280×720 and replaced by the sub-stream when still too heavy. |
| Detection hold (s) | `number` | No | How long a detection stays on after the last event the camera sent. Cameras repeat their events while something moves: one scene trigger per detection, not per repeat. |
| Health check interval (s) | `number` | No | How often each device is checked: reachable or not, cameras online, alarm outputs and detection switches. |
| Detailed logs (debug) | `boolean` | No | Log every event the devices send. Turn it on to understand why a detection does not show up, then off again: it is verbose. Passwords are never logged. |

## How to install Hikvision in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Hikvision appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-hikvision:0.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-hikvision](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-hikvision).

Hikvision requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Hikvision is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
